hook.text: Norovirus causes 685 million cases of gastroenteritis per year worldwide. It's the most common foodborne illness.

buildup.text: It spreads through contaminated food, water, and surfaces. A single infected food handler can sicken hundreds.

discovery.text: Just 18 viral particles can cause infection—far fewer than any bacterial pathogen. It's incredibly contagious.

twist.text: Norovirus survives hand sanitizer. Alcohol-based gels don't kill it. Only soap and water remove it effectively.

climax.text: Cruise ship outbreaks made headlines, but 60% of norovirus outbreaks actually start in restaurants and catering.

punchline.text: 18 particles. That's all it takes. Wash your hands with soap, not gel.

quiz.question: Why doesn't hand sanitizer work well against norovirus?
options: Norovirus survives alcohol—only soap and water effectively remove it
